----------------------------------------------------------------
 EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN
----------------------------------------------------------------

1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY  
Method: Fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity Design (FRD) combined with 2-stage least squares (local RD-IV).

Why it fits:  
• Regulation creates a sharp cutoff in the pension-funding ratio (assets ÷ liabilities). Falling below the statutory threshold (≈ 0.90) triggers legally mandated minimum cash contributions.  
• Crossing the threshold is plausibly exogenous to short-run real-investment opportunities, so observations infinitesimally close to the cutoff are comparable.  
• Because compliance is imperfect (some firms top-up even when slightly above, or delay when slightly below), the cutoff delivers a jump in the probability—not certainty—of high pension contributions ⇒ “fuzzy”.  
• We use the indicator “Below threshold” as an instrument for the actual dollar amount of pension contributions and estimate its causal effect on corporate investment.

2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL  

Treatment variable (endogenous):  
  PensionContribution_it  ≡ cash contributions to DB plan in year t, scaled by beginning-of-year assets.

Instrument (exogenous “treatment assignment”):  
  Treat_it  = 1 { FundingRatio_it < 0.90 }.

Control group:  
  Firms with FundingRatio just above 0.90 within a symmetric bandwidth (e.g., ±8 ppts) form the counterfactual.

Running variable:  
  FundingRatio_it = PlanAssets/ProjectedBenefitObligation.

Cutoff: c = 0.90 (or 1.0 if legally binding year differs—use statutory value in force that year).

Timing:  
  Assignment occurs at the fiscal year-end valuation of the pension plan; investment is measured the following fiscal year so that contributions precede investment.

3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS  

A1 (Continuity): All other determinants of investment are smooth in FundingRatio at c.  
  Plausibility: Managers have limited ability to fine-tune actuarial assumptions precisely enough to “land” on either side within ±1–2 ppts.

A2 (No precise manipulation): Firms cannot sort exactly around 0.90.  
  Plausibility: Funding ratios depend on market returns and actuarial valuations that are noisy at an annual frequency.

A3 (Local exclusion): The indicator Treat_it affects investment only through its impact on pension contributions (first stage).  
  Plausibility: Regulation mandates cash payments but does not impose additional investment-related rules.

A4 (First-stage relevance): Crossing the cutoff generates a sizable jump in contributions.  
  Plausibility: Established in prior descriptive work; can be verified empirically (F-stat > 10).

A5 (Stable unit treatment value / no spillovers): One firm’s funding status does not influence another’s investment within the narrow window.  
  Plausibility: Reasonable given firm-level decision making.

4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION  

T1 Precise manipulation of FundingRatio  
  • Test: McCrary density test; histogram of FundingRatio.  
  • Fix: “Donut” RD—drop firms within ±1 ppt; show results stable.

T2 Other discontinuous rules at the same threshold (e.g., PBGC premiums jump)  
  • Collect statutory information; control for contemporaneous PBGC premium changes; run placebo cutoffs at 0.80 and 1.00.

T3 Mean reversion in corporate performance (underfunded firms may also be in downturns)  
  • Include controls for lagged ROA, Tobin’s q, sales growth.  
  • Use narrow bandwidths and firm fixed effects in a panel RD specification.

5. R CODE OUTLINE  

```r
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# -------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table); library(fixest); library(rdrobust); library(ivreg)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and merge data
# -------------------------------------------------------------
fin  <- fread("financials.csv")           # Compustat-like
pens <- fread("pension_filings.csv")      # Form 5500 / 10-K pension footnotes
stk  <- fread("crsp_stock.csv")           # Optional market controls

dat  <- merge(fin, pens, by = c("gvkey","fyear"))
dat  <- merge(dat, stk,  by = c("gvkey","fyear"), all.x = TRUE)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Construct variables
# -------------------------------------------------------------
dat[, funding_ratio := plan_assets / pbo]                       # running var
dat[, treat := as.integer(funding_ratio < 0.90)]                # assignment
dat[, contrib := pension_contrib / total_assets]                # endogenous
dat[, invest  := capx / lag(total_assets)]                      # outcome
dat[, running_c := funding_ratio - 0.90]                        # centered R

# Keep only DB plan firms with non-missing key vars
dat <- dat[!is.na(funding_ratio) & !is.na(invest)]

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Bandwidth selection (Imbens–Kalyanaraman)
# -------------------------------------------------------------
bw <- IKbandwidth(dat$running_c, dat$treat)   # rdrobust helper

# Restrict sample to chosen bandwidth
sample <- dat[abs(running_c) <= bw]

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. MAIN SPECIFICATION: Fuzzy RD-IV
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 1st stage
fs <- feols(contrib ~ treat + poly(running_c,2) | gvkey + fyear, 
            data = sample, cluster = "gvkey")

# 2nd stage (local 2SLS)
rd_iv <- feols(invest ~ 1 | treat + poly(running_c,2) | gvkey + fyear, 
               data = sample, cluster = "gvkey")

summary(fs)
summary(rd_iv)

# rdrobust implementation (alternative)
rd_res <- rdrobust(y = sample$invest,
                   x = sample$running_c,
                   c = 0, fuzzy = sample$treat)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Robustness: donut RD (drop ±1 ppt)
# -------------------------------------------------------------
donut <- sample[abs(running_c) > 0.01]      # 0.01 = 1 percentage point
rd_iv_donut <- feols(invest ~ 1 | treat + poly(running_c,2) | gvkey + fyear,
                     data = donut, cluster = "gvkey")
summary(rd_iv_donut)
```

6. EXPECTED RESULTS  

Theory predicts that when cash must be diverted to pension plans, internally financed investment falls. Empirical estimates in related settings suggest the pass-through is incomplete. I expect:  
  β_IV ≈ –0.25 to –0.40  
meaning a 1 %-of-assets increase in pension contributions lowers investment by roughly 0.25–0.40 %-of-assets.

7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (RD)  

C1 Running-variable density smooth?   1  
C2 Covariates smooth at cutoff?       1  
C3 No other discontinuities?          0 (PBGC premiums possible, but testable)  
C4 Strong first stage (F > 10)?       1  
C5 Functional-form/bandwidth robustness? 1  

Total = 4 / 5 → generally credible but must address C3 explicitly.
